definitions.meaning: first meaning: an affectionate name for a mischievous little one
second meaning: a tricky situation or mess

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster has landed in trouble again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troublesome child in predicament' reads as one story, but it splits at 'in' into two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a scamp is called a little one of this name, and being in a tight spot is also described with the same word.

clue.text: Eccentric type after job mailed item

indicators.note: after says the job's word comes first and the eccentric's word follows it

parts.note: a post is a job or position
a card is an amusing, eccentric person

explanation.surface: An oddball has just been given a job, perhaps in the post room.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture card sent through the mail is a classic example of an item posted to someone.

clue.text: Fashion designer pinning first of gems on a knitted garment

indicators.note: the designer's name pins the other letters, holding them fast inside it
in a down clue, on places one piece directly above the next
first of asks only for the opening letter of the word gems

explanation.surface: A couturier fixes jewels onto a woollen top with pins.
explanation.walkthrough: G above A makes GA, which goes inside CARDIN to give CARDIGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This button-front sweater, named after an Earl, is a knitted woollen garment worn open or fastened.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to secure or obtain, as when you secure a job
second meaning: real estate, earth that someone owns

explanation.surface: Someone wants to buy a plot of real estate.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something can be to secure it like a fish, and owned terrain is called by the same short word.

clue.text: Fighter in soup, what a mess!

indicators.note: a mess is something jumbled and disordered, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a fly, or a boxer, in their soup: what a mess!
explanation.walkthrough: 'what a mess!' reads as an exclamation, but 'what' is fodder and 'a mess' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-handed boxer is called by this term, so the word names a kind of fighter in the ring.

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: sunlight comes down from a clear sky
second meaning: the idiom for something sudden and unexpected

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic, literal reading of the idiom: rays of light come down from the sky's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes events arriving suddenly and unexpectedly, like a bolt from a clear sky.

clue.text: Container for wine served with a fish

indicators.note: served with means one thing comes alongside another, so the pieces are placed together

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A carafe of wine accompanies a fish course at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: This large ocean species is a well-known food fish, often canned or served as steak.

parts.note: a plan is a design or scheme

explanation.surface: A science-fiction writer designs an alien world.
explanation.definitionFit: A world orbiting a star is a body of this kind, like Mars or Earth.

clue.text: Car, where wife put on shoes

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on places the wife's letter on top of the next piece

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: In the car, a wife slips her shoes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on shoes' looks like getting dressed; here it places W above HEELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a car or vehicle, as in 'got some new set of these', is this informal plural.

clue.text: Fiddle about right for its cord?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a sting is a swindle or fiddle
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A violinist asks what is right to fit as the instrument's cord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' wants to be the violin, and in the end it is: 'its cord' refers back to it, though in the wordplay a fiddle is a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin's sounding cords are its gut or wire lines stretched along the neck and bowed.

clue.text: Very old style adopted by philosopher

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the philosopher's word takes the style's word inside

parts.note: a sage is a wise thinker

explanation.surface: A philosopher takes up an old-fashioned style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by philosopher' reads like a thinker embracing a fashion, but the sage's letters simply take in the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Used humorously as an adjective, the prehistoric period's name means ancient or hopelessly outdated.

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters before it are formed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A fast new computer program for notes is a handy piece of software.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicating text and inserting it elsewhere is a basic computing function found in every editor and program.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to copy or plagiarise someone's work

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a crime involving a bed; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy dishonestly from another is to use their work this way, and a cot for an infant bears the same name.

clue.text: Spoil opening of film after error

indicators.note: after places the film's letter behind the error's word

parts.note: a goof is a silly blunder

indicators.note: opening of asks only for the first letter of the word film

explanation.surface: A gaffe ruins a movie premiere.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that turns bad or rots can be described with this phrasal verb, meaning it has spoilt.

clue.text: Bit of white, a little colour

indicators.note: bit of means only a portion of the following words is used, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the words, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: A painter adds a touch of white to make a slightly different shade.
explanation.walkthrough: whiTE A Little holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark greenish-blue shade, named after a duck, is a recognised paint colour.

indicators.note: it's said means we hear the word spoken rather than see it written

explanation.surface: Gossip that some labourer is a nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: Something small and of little importance is described by this adjective, the opposite of major.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to obtain or gain, as goals or points
second meaning: a group of twenty

explanation.walkthrough: 'Net twenty' looks like a sum after deductions; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain or achieve a goal is to obtain it, and the old counting word for a group of a score is twenty.

clue.text: Tossing and turning irately, European heard wake-up call

indicators.note: tossing and turning means restless movement, so the letters are thrown about into a new order
heard means the word for the European is spoken, and we write what we hear

parts.note: a Czech is from the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: An angry insomniac tosses all night until a foreign neighbour's alarm goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: A jolting reminder of how things truly are acts as an alarm that shakes someone out of illusion.

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone names a stirring English song, perhaps the Beatles' Help!
explanation.walkthrough: ESONGAID read upwards gives the answer; the exclamation mark belongs to the Beatles title in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor pins down an illness by name, so to identify a condition is the same as this medical verb.

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something done in an extraordinary way, so the letters are rearranged unusually

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that a sea creature really is enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: This Atlantic pinniped species is a sea-dwelling animal of the seal family, so it is a marine mammal.

clue.text: Hollow roar breaking boundaries when flying — at this?

definitions.text: Hollow roar breaking boundaries when flying — at this?

indicators.note: breaking smashes the word apart so its letters can be rebuilt in another order
flying suggests letters scattered through the air before landing in a fresh order
something hollow has had its insides removed, so only the outside letters of roar remain

explanation.surface: A jet breaks through limits in flight with a hollow boom.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the 'roar' is the sonic boom heard when a plane passes Mach one, the limit 'broken' in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The sudden surge in drag near Mach one was the obstacle aviators had to break, producing a sonic boom.

indicators.note: up the wall means driven crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tools are handed up to someone working on top of a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the wall' reads like a direction for passing things; it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden digging implements with a flat blade, used for turning soil, are common hand tools.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to tremble or quiver
second meaning: a musical note half a crotchet long

explanation.walkthrough: A crotchet is the British name for a quarter note; this note is an eighth note.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice that trembles is said to waver this way, and in music the eighth note has the same name.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stop up a hole
second meaning: a mention promoting something, as on a chat show

explanation.walkthrough: The two parts are unrelated meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopper that seals a sink is this word, and a free promotional mention for a product is too.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rabbit on is British slang for chatter on and on
second meaning: a stream of liquid gushing out

explanation.surface: A bunny rides on a jet aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit on is British slang for talking at tedious length.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk at length pompously is to hold forth this way, and a gush of water from a nozzle is also called this.

clue.text: Margaret has missed starter — like a frittata?

indicators.note: has missed starter means the name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Peggy is a pet form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret skipped the first course and went straight to the omelette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a dinner course; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A frittata is an Italian omelette, so it tastes of or is made from beaten hen's produce.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tab or tag of material hanging loose
second meaning: a state of agitation, as in 'in a stew'

explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like food but means a fluster.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging tab of material can be called this, and nervous panic or fluster is also known by the word.

clue.text: Eyeball, optical globe looking everywhere initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: An eye roams around in all directions.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to stare at someone openly and lecherously is to look them over intently.

indicators.note: in places the sin's word inside the other word

parts.note: a dish is an attractive person, and Adonis was a beautiful youth

explanation.surface: There is something wicked about a handsome young man.
explanation.walkthrough: Adonis, the beautiful youth of Greek myth, stands for any good-looking man, which slang calls a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fiendish or diabolical is cruel and malicious, so it means extremely bad.

clue.text: Slight backtracking later on, girl admits

indicators.note: backtracking means going the opposite way, so the letters are read from right to left
admits means the letters are let in and contained within the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the words, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: A girl owns up to having slighted someone, retracting it later on.
explanation.walkthrough: laTER ON GIrl holds ERONGI, which reads backwards as IGNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub or disregard someone is to deliberately take no notice of them, so it means to treat with disdain.

clue.text: Short of money, son unable to get out

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
trapped means stuck with no exit

explanation.surface: A broke son is stuck at home, unable to move out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being strapped for cash is an informal way to say someone is hard up and lacking funds.

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the party's word goes around the other piece

explanation.surface: A party features a show of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside REV-EL.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose or display something hidden is to uncover it, so the verb means to make visible.
